html:
Krak des Chevaliers is a castle in western Syria, on a hill guarding the gap between the coast and the interior. The Knights Hospitaller held it from 1142 and made it one of the strongest fortresses of the Middle Ages.

They rebuilt it with two rings of walls, round towers and a great sloping base, and up to two thousand men could hold it. It survived many attacks, including by Saladin. In 1271 the Mamluk sultan Baybars took it after a siege of about a month, by tricking the defenders with a forged letter.

T. E. Lawrence called it perhaps the best preserved and most wholly admirable castle in the world. It became a World Heritage Site in 2006 and was damaged by bombing in the Syrian civil war. See also the Crusader states and Kerak.
